podcast.title: Major Label Status and Johnny Otis Signing (1957)
podcast.body: Capital Records was recognized as one of the biggest record labels in the United States. Johnny Otis secured a contract with Capital in 1957, ensuring him major label distribution for the first time in many years, largely due to the advocacy of comedian Mickey Katz. "Cats was on capital, one of the biggest labels in the country and so for the first time in many years Otis had guaranteed major label distribution for his records."

podcast.title: Signing and Dropping of Virtual Rapper FM Mecha (2022)
podcast.body: Capital Records signed virtual rapper FM Mecha in August 2022 and released the single "Florida Water." However, the label subsequently dropped FM Mecha due to significant backlash and criticism from the public, who viewed the character as a caricature of Black culture created by non-Black individuals. "In August 2022, capital records signed FM Mecha and released a single entitled Florida Water."

podcast.title: Agreement Breakage
podcast.body: The Beach Boys eventually broke their agreement with Capital Records following the cancellation of the Smile project, subsequently signing with Warner Bros. "Después de romper su acuerdo con Capital."

podcast.title: Bonnie Raitt Signing (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt signed with Capital Records in the late 1980s after getting sober. This move preceded the release of her highly successful and Grammy-winning album "Nick of Time," which Capital helped promote to adult contemporary radio. "She had battled drug and alcohol addiction, got sober in the late 80s and signed to a new label, Capital Records."

podcast.title: Extensive Promotion of Smile
podcast.body: Capital Records initially provided strong backing for Brian Wilson and the Smile project, even hiring Derek Taylor, former press chief for The Beatles, to promote Wilson as a musical genius. The label actively advertised Smile, predicting over a million sales by January 1967 and printing more than 400,000 album covers in anticipation. "Capito le empezó a promocionar el disco en prensa, llegando a baticinar que en enero venderían más de un millón de copias."

podcast.title: Financial Costs from Smile Delays
podcast.body: Brian Wilson's erratic behavior during the Smile production, such as repeatedly canceling sessions with assembled musicians, incurred significant financial costs for Capital Records, contributing to the strain on the project. "cancelaba sesiones con los músicos de arreonidos, cosa que costó mucho dinero a Capital."

podcast.title: Smile Album Release Agreement
podcast.body: Capital Records reached an agreement with The Beach Boys for the Smile album to be released on January 15, 1967. This provided a tight deadline of merely three months to capitalize on the significant hype generated by the "Good Vibrations" single. "los bichsboys llegaron a un acuerdo con Capital Records, acordando que ese nuevo disco saldría la venta al 15 de enero de 1967."
